docs.title: What is judicial_common_space?
docs.text: judicial_common_space computes the Judicial Common Space (JCS) score of every appointment of a federal judge who has served since 1953 (the first year of the original study, or any year you choose), following Epstein, Martin, Segal, and Westerland, "The Judicial Common Space," 23 J.L. Econ. & Org. 303 (2007). It saves them in a spreadsheet with each judge's name, the Federal Judicial Center's two numbers for the judge (nid and jid), and the judge's score for each appointment, and checks them against the published scores.

docs.title: Why use judicial_common_space?
docs.text:
This package:

  • Scores every Article III appointment: district courts, courts of appeals, and the Supreme Court.
  • Uses the current sources, downloaded when needed: the Federal Judicial Center's Biographical Directory of Article III Federal Judges, Voteview's DW-NOMINATE scores, the congress-legislators dates of senators' service, the Martin-Quinn scores, and Wikipedia's articles on the courts of appeals (for circuit judges' duty stations).
  • Shows its work: each row says which state the judge was appointed from, how that was found, and which senators (or the president) the score came from.
  • Checks itself against the published JCS scores of circuit judges and justices and against Christina Boyd's scores of district judges, which are made the same way.

docs.title: How the scores are made
docs.text:
The paper scores the lower courts by the rule of Giles, Hettinger, and Peppers (2001), which follows the norm of senatorial courtesy. If a judge is appointed from a state where the president and at least one senator are of the same party, the judge gets that senator's NOMINATE score, or the mean of the senators' scores. Otherwise the judge gets the president's score. Justices get their Martin-Quinn score in each term, put on the same scale by the paper's arctangent transformation: 2/π · arctan(b0 + b1 · MQ).

The package applies the rule this way:

Step How Appointment Each row of the center's file of federal judicial service. The senators and the president are those of the nomination (or of the recess appointment, if there was no nomination). A judge renominated by a new president after a recess appointment (as Roger Gregory was) is scored by the president who nominated the judge to the Senate. A judge moved to a court without an appointment (as the Fifth Circuit's judges were to the Eleventh in 1981) keeps the score of the appointment before. Home state A district judge's comes from the court's name. A circuit judge's is the state of a district court in the circuit that the judge served on before; or else of the job the judge held when appointed (or the most recent before), as the center's record of the judge's career names it; or else of the judge's duty station, as Wikipedia's article on the court gives it; or else the judge's birth state, if it is in the circuit. The duty station comes after the career because it is where the judge sat, which is sometimes not where the judge came from, but it agrees with the state from the career for 98.5% of the judges who have both. (The state of the judge whom the appointee replaced, from the center's seat numbers, made the matches worse: a seat changes states about one time in five.) Judges of the District of Columbia Circuit, the Federal Circuit, and the other national courts get the president's score, as they do in the published scores. Senators By default, every senator from the state who sat in the Congress of the appointment and belonged to the president's party, as the published scores count them (--senators congress). With --senators date, only the senators who held the seats on the day, by their party on that day, which is the rule as the paper states it and closer to Boyd's district scores. Scores Voteview's nominate_dim1 for senators and presidents (one score for each member's whole service). Justices The arctangent transformation with the coefficients of the 2024 release of the JCS scores (b0 = 0.1934, b1 = 0.6025), recovered from its 782 justice-terms (r = 0.9998), because both scales have changed since the paper estimated b0 = −0.1736 and b1 = 0.461 from the scores of 2005 (--transformation paper uses those). A justice's appointment gets the score of its first term, and the "Justices" sheet has every term.

docs.title: How well they match the published scores
docs.text:
With the default settings, against the JCS 2024 release and Boyd's district court scores (through the 118th Congress):

Check Published Found Same (within 0.0005) Same or within 0.02 Correlation Circuit judges (JCS 2024) 705 703 88.3% 96.9% 0.998 District judges (Boyd) 2,615 2,615 83.6% 95.4% 0.998 Justice-terms (JCS 2024) 782 782 24.9% 99.4% 1.000

With --senators date, the district judges match Boyd's scores 99.2% of the time (within 0.02) and the circuit judges match the JCS scores 93.2% of the time, so the two published sources count senators differently.

Most differences under 0.02 are not errors. Voteview re-estimates the score of every member who is still serving whenever it adds a Congress, so judges whose senators are still in office (Fetterman, Rick Scott, Hickenlooper, and others) drift a little from scores published with an older file. The same is true of recent justices in the Martin-Quinn scores. The larger differences that remain are judges whom the published file places in a state that neither the center's records nor Wikipedia show (such as Richard Cudahy in Illinois and Stephen Trott in Idaho), a few D.C. Circuit judges and the Federal Circuit judges who came from the Court of Customs and Patent Appeals, which the published file scores differently, and some possible slips in the published files. The spreadsheet's check sheets list every comparison, and the next section explains every one that differs by more than 0.05.

docs.title: Using the published scores
docs.text:
--use-published (off by default) gives a judge or a justice's term the published score wherever it differs from the computed one by more than 0.05 (or --published-threshold): Epstein et al.'s for circuit judges and justices, and Boyd's for district judges. The Scores and Justices sheets then say where each score came from (jcs_source) and keep the computed score beside it (computed_jcs); the check sheets still compare the computed scores. With the default settings, it replaces the scores of 95 appointments since 1953 (80 district judges, 14 circuit judges, and Justice Jackson's appointment, from her first term) and of two justice-terms; with --senators date, it replaces 46 (13 district judges, 32 circuit judges, and Justice Jackson's).

Use it to reproduce the published scores, as when a study must line up with earlier work that used them. It is off by default because:

  • The two sources count senators differently (Boyd by the day, Epstein et al. by the Congress), so taking both mixes their rules: with either setting of --senators, one of them is overruled.
  • Some of the published scores that it would take look like slips, such as John Nalbandian's, Morris Arnold's, James Connell's, and the six New York and Kentucky judges'.
  • Only judges in the published files can be replaced, so judges appointed in the same circumstances can end up with scores made by different rules.
  • The published scores were made with older Voteview files, so they lag behind the current scores of senators who are still serving.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install judicial_common_space, use pip:

pip install judicial-common-space

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
From the command line:

judicial-common-space --output judicial_common_space.xlsx

Or from Python:

import judicial_common_space

judicial_common_space.run('judicial_common_space.xlsx', start_year = 1953)
Option Default Description --output judicial_common_space.xlsx Where to save the spreadsheet. --start-year 1953 Include judges who served on a court in this year or later, and the justices' terms from the one sitting in January of that year. The default is the first year of the original study, which covered 1953 through 2000; the published scores now run through 2024, and these through the latest data. --senators congress Which senators count: congress (as the published scores do) or date (those holding the seats on the day). --transformation jcs2024 How Martin-Quinn scores are put on the scale: jcs2024 or paper. --martin-quinn the data folder's The Martin-Quinn justices.csv, if it cannot be downloaded. The Martin-Quinn site checks for automated browsers, so if the download fails, save the file from its page and pass its path (or put it in the data folder's politics folder). --data-folder data/courts beside the code folder Where the downloads are kept: the same folders that courtpy uses, so the projects share them. Set JUDICIAL_COMMON_SPACE_DATA_DIR to change it for good. --overwrite off Download the files again, as when the center has added judges or Voteview has added votes. --no-download off Use only the files that are already there. --use-published off Use the published score (Epstein et al.'s for circuit judges and justices, Boyd's for district judges) where it differs from the computed one by more than the threshold (see Using the published scores). --published-threshold 0.05 The largest difference from a published score that keeps the computed score, with --use-published. --no-check off Do not compare the scores with the published scores.

The spreadsheet has these sheets:

Sheet Contents Scores A row for each appointment: judge, nid, jid, the court, the president and party, the dates, the Congress, home_state (a postal code) and state_source (how it was found), duty_station (Wikipedia's state for a circuit judge), method and senators (how the score was found), president_score, computed_jcs, jcs, and jcs_source ("computed", or with --use-published, "Epstein et al." or "Boyd"). Justices Each justice's Martin-Quinn and JCS scores in each term, with computed_jcs and jcs_source. Verification The agreement with each set of published scores. Circuit check, District check, Justice check Every comparison, with both scores and how the computed one was found. About The method, the sources, and the settings.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

• Computed the Judicial Common Space score of every appointment of a federal judge who served since 1953 (the first year of Epstein et al.'s study), from the Federal Judicial Center's Biographical Directory, Voteview's DW-NOMINATE scores, the dates of senators' service, and the Martin-Quinn scores
  • Saved the scores in a spreadsheet with both of the center's numbers for each judge (nid and jid)
  • Checked the scores against the published JCS scores of circuit judges and justices and Christina Boyd's scores of district judges
  • Added the judicial-common-space command
  • Found the home states of circuit judges whose careers show none from their duty stations in Wikipedia's articles on the courts of appeals, and added the duty_station column
  • Added --use-published, which uses Epstein et al.'s or Boyd's score where it differs from the computed one by more than 0.05 (--published-threshold), and the computed_jcs and jcs_source columns
  • Explained every score that differs from the published ones by more than 0.05 in the README

docs.title: Style Guidelines
docs.text:
This package follows the Google Python Style Guide with two notable exceptions:

  1. It always adds spaces around "=". This not only violates the Google guide, it violates PEP8, the foundational Python style guide from which all other resources are derived. I defy this strong, long-standing norm because I find it more readable. My brain and eyes have trouble seeing two separate objects when an equal sign is in the middle. I imagine that I am not alone in this accessibility issue. Further, as PEP8 itself notes, required spaces around equal signs are becoming increasing common with type annotations becoming part of best practices (and, as a result, signatures to classes, functions, and methods regularly include spaces around the equal signs). I realize that this will seem alien to many coders, but it is far easier on my eyes.
  2. I use some so-called "power features", primarily dunder methods, to make my interfaces easier to access and use. This is disfavored in the Google Python Style Guide because such code is often more difficult for others to read. To address that concern, I try to document and comment as to what the code is doing whenever I used any of the "power features" of Python.

Because of the first exception, the project does not use a code formatter (such as ruff format), which would remove those spaces.

docs.text:
Returns the scores of the appointments and of the justices.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default files dict[str, Path]

the path of each file, by its kind (see sources.paths).

required senators str

which senators count, "congress" or "date" (see politics.Senate.senators). Defaults to "congress".

'congress' martin_quinn Path | str | None

the file of the justices' Martin-Quinn scores. Defaults to None, in which case the one in the data folder is used if there is one.

None transformation str

the transformation of Martin-Quinn scores, "jcs2024" or "paper" (see politics.justices). Defaults to "jcs2024".

'jcs2024'

Returns:

Type Description tuple[DataFrame, DataFrame]

The scores of every appointment (see scores.appointments), and of every justice in every term (see scores.justices), which is empty if there are no Martin-Quinn scores. Without the file of duty stations, a judge whose career shows no state has the judge's birth state.

Source code in src/judicial_common_space/main.py 
def compute(
    files: dict[str, pathlib.Path],
    *,
    senators: str = 'congress',
    martin_quinn: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    transformation: str = 'jcs2024') -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Returns the scores of the appointments and of the justices.

    Args:
        files: the path of each file, by its kind (see `sources.paths`).
        senators: which senators count, "congress" or "date" (see
            `politics.Senate.senators`). Defaults to "congress".
        martin_quinn: the file of the justices' Martin-Quinn scores.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case the one in the data folder is
            used if there is one.
        transformation: the transformation of Martin-Quinn scores, "jcs2024"
            or "paper" (see `politics.justices`). Defaults to "jcs2024".

    Returns:
        The scores of every appointment (see `scores.appointments`), and of
            every justice in every term (see `scores.justices`), which is
            empty if there are no Martin-Quinn scores. Without the file of
            duty stations, a judge whose career shows no state has the
            judge's birth state.

    """
    table = fjc.appointments(files['service'], files['demographics'])
    careers = fjc.careers(files['career'])
    found: dict[tuple[int, str], str] = {}
    if files['duty_stations'].is_file():
        found = stations.match(
            table, stations.duty_stations(files['duty_stations']))
    else:
        logger.warning(
            'there are no duty stations at %s, so judges whose careers show '
            'no state have their birth states', files['duty_stations'])
    table['duty_station'] = [
        found.get((nid, court)) for nid, court in zip(
            table['nid'], table['court'], strict = True)]
    senate = politics.Senate.from_files(
        files['congress'],
        [files['legislators_historical'], files['legislators_current']])
    path = pathlib.Path(martin_quinn) if martin_quinn else files['martin_quinn']
    terms = pd.DataFrame()
    if path.is_file():

            politics.justices(path, transformation), table, start_year = 0)
    else:
        logger.warning(
            'there are no Martin-Quinn scores at %s, so the justices have no '
            'scores: save "justices.csv" from %s there', path, options._MQ_PAGE)
    scored = scores.appointments(
        table, careers, senate, start_year = None, senators = senators,
        terms = terms)
    return scored, terms

def run(
    output: pathlib.Path | str = 'judicial_common_space.xlsx',
    *,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    start_year: int = options._START_YEAR,
    senators: str = 'congress',
    martin_quinn: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    transformation: str = 'jcs2024',
    use_published: bool = False,
    published_threshold: float = verify._PUBLISHED_THRESHOLD,
    download: bool = True,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    check: bool = True,
    session: Any = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Downloads the files that are missing, computes and checks the scores.

    Then it writes the spreadsheet (see `export.write`).

    Args:
        output: where to save the spreadsheet. Defaults to
            "judicial_common_space.xlsx" in the current folder.
        folder: the data folder. Defaults to `None`, in which case
            `utilities.data_folder()` is used.
        start_year: the first year of service to include (see
            `scores.appointments`). Defaults to 1953, the first year of
            Epstein et al.'s study. The justices' terms begin with the one
            that was sitting in January of that year (the 1952 term, for
            1953), as the study's do.
        senators: which senators count, "congress" or "date" (see
            `politics.Senate.senators`). Defaults to "congress", as in the
            published Judicial Common Space scores.
        martin_quinn: the file of the justices' Martin-Quinn scores.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case the one in the data folder is
            used, which is downloaded if it can be.
        transformation: the transformation of Martin-Quinn scores, "jcs2024"
            (as in the 2024 release of the scores) or "paper" (Epstein et
            al.'s of 2007; see `politics.justices`). Defaults to "jcs2024".
        use_published: whether to use the published score of a judge (or a
            justice's term) where it differs from the computed one by more
            than `published_threshold` (see `verify.use_published`). The
            checks still compare the computed scores. Defaults to `False`.
        published_threshold: the largest difference from a published score
            that keeps the computed score. Defaults to 0.05.
        download: whether to download the files that are missing. Defaults
            to `True`.
        overwrite: whether to download the files again even if they are
            there. Defaults to `False`.
        check: whether to compare the scores with published scores.
            Defaults to `True`.
        session: an object with a `get` method like a `requests.Session`.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case a `requests.Session` is made.

    Returns:
        The path of the spreadsheet.

    """
    files = sources.paths(folder)
    if download:
        session = utilities.open_session(session)
        sources.download(
            _INPUTS, folder, overwrite = overwrite, session = session)
        optional = ['duty_stations'] + ([] if martin_quinn else ['martin_quinn'])
        optional += list(_PUBLISHED) if check or use_published else []
        for kind in optional:
            try:
                sources.download(
                    kind, folder, overwrite = overwrite, session = session)
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                logger.warning('could not download %s: %s', kind, error)
    scored, terms = compute(
        files, senators = senators, martin_quinn = martin_quinn,
        transformation = transformation)
    checks = _checks(files, scored, terms) if check or use_published else {}
    if use_published:
        if not checks:
            logger.warning(
                'there are no published scores in %s, so every score is '
                'computed', files['jcs_judges'].parent)
        scored, terms = verify.use_published(
            scored, terms, checks, published_threshold)
        replaced = int((_since(scored, start_year)['jcs_source'] != (
            'computed')).sum())
        logger.info(
            'used the published scores of %d appointments that differ by '
            'more than %.2f', replaced, published_threshold)
    else:
        scored, terms = verify.mark_computed(scored), verify.mark_computed(
            terms)
    sheets: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {
        'Scores': _since(scored, start_year),
        # A term begins in October, so the one sitting in January of the
        # first year began the year before.
        'Justices': (
            terms[terms['term'] >= start_year - 1] if not terms.empty
            else terms)}
    if check:
        sheets['Verification'] = verify.summarize(checks)
        names = {
            'circuit_judges': 'Circuit check',
            'district_judges': 'District check',
            'justices': 'Justice check'}
        sheets.update({names[name]: table for name, table in checks.items()})
        for row in sheets['Verification'].to_dict('records'):
            logger.info(
                '%s: %d of %d found; %.1f%% the same and %.1f%% the same or '
                'within %.2f', row['check'], row['found'], row['published'],
                100 * row['share_same'], 100 * row['share_same_or_close'],
                verify._CLOSE)
    settings = {
        'start_year': start_year, 'senators': senators,
        'transformation': transformation,
        'use_published': (
            f'{use_published} (threshold {published_threshold})'
            if use_published else use_published),
        'appointments': len(sheets['Scores'])}
    path = export.write(output, sheets, settings)
    missing = int(sheets['Scores']['jcs'].isna().sum())
    logger.info(
        'wrote %d appointments to %s (%d without a score)',
        len(sheets['Scores']), path, missing)
    return path

def write(
    path: pathlib.Path | str,
    sheets: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame],
    settings: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Writes the scores and their checks to a spreadsheet.

    Args:
        path: where to save the spreadsheet (an Excel ".xlsx" file). Its
            folder is created if needed.
        sheets: the tables to write, by the name of each sheet. Empty
            tables are left out.
        settings: the settings that the scores were made with, which are
            listed on the "About" sheet. Defaults to `None`.

    Returns:
        `path`.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path).expanduser()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    about = list(_ABOUT)
    if settings:
        about += ['', 'Settings:']
        about += [f'{name}: {value}' for name, value in settings.items()]
    with pd.ExcelWriter(path, engine = 'openpyxl') as writer:
        for name, table in sheets.items():
            if table is None or table.empty:
                continue
            table.to_excel(writer, sheet_name = name, index = False)
            sheet = writer.sheets[name]
            sheet.freeze_panes = 'A2'
            for number, column in enumerate(table.columns, start = 1):
                # A column with no values (as the district judges' duty
                # stations) is as wide as its name.
                lengths = [
                    0 if pd.isna(value) else len(str(value))
                    for value in table[column]]
                widest = int(pd.Series(lengths).quantile(0.9)) if lengths else 0
                width = max(len(str(column)), widest) + 2
                letter = sheet.cell(row = 1, column = number).column_letter
                sheet.column_dimensions[letter].width = min(width, 60)
        pd.DataFrame({'About': about}).to_excel(
            writer, sheet_name = 'About', index = False)
        writer.sheets['About'].column_dimensions['A'].width = 120
    return path

def appointments(
    service: pd.DataFrame | pathlib.Path | str,
    demographics: pd.DataFrame | pathlib.Path | str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns a row for each court that each judge served on.

    | Column | Meaning |
    | --- | --- |
    | `nid`, `jid` | The Federal Judicial Center's two numbers for the judge. |
    | `judge` | The judge's name, as the center reports it ("Last, First Middle"). |
    | `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix` | Its parts. |
    | `sequence` | The order of the judge's service on this court among the judge's courts. |
    | `court_type`, `court`, `title` | The court's type and name, and the judge's title on it. |
    | `circuit` | The number of a court of appeals (12 for the District of Columbia Circuit and 13 for the Federal Circuit). Missing for other courts. |
    | `president`, `party` | The president who appointed the judge and that president's party. A judge whose recess appointment was confirmed after a new president nominated the judge again (as Roger Gregory was) has the president who nominated the judge to the Senate. |
    | `recess_date`, `nomination_date`, `confirmation_date`, `commission_date`, `termination_date` | The dates of the appointment and of the end of the service, as YYYY-MM-DD. Blank if there was none. |
    | `appointment_date` | The date that the judge's senators and president are found on: the nomination, or the recess appointment, confirmation, or commission if there was no nomination. |
    | `reassigned` | Whether the judge was moved to the court without an appointment, in which case the judge has the president and dates of the appointment before. |
    | `earlier` | The courts that the judge served on before, as a tuple of their names. |
    | `birth_state` | The postal code of the state where the judge was born. |

    Args:
        service: the file of federal judicial service, as a path or a table.
        demographics: the file of demographics, as a path or a table.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if a file lacks a column that is needed.

    Returns:
        The table, sorted by the judges' numbers and then by the order of
            each judge's service.

    """
    served = _read(service)
    people = _read(demographics)
    _require(
        served,
        ['nid', 'Sequence', 'Appointing President',
         'Party of Appointing President', *_COLUMNS],
        'the file of federal judicial service')
    _require(
        people,
        ['nid', 'jid', 'Last Name', 'First Name', 'Middle Name', 'Suffix',
         'Birth State'],
        'the file of demographics')
    served = served.assign(
        nid = served['nid'].astype(int),
        sequence = pd.to_numeric(served['Sequence'], errors = 'coerce'))
    served = served.sort_values(['nid', 'sequence'], kind = 'stable')
    served = served.reset_index(drop = True)
    table = served[list(_COLUMNS)].rename(columns = _COLUMNS)
    table.insert(0, 'nid', served['nid'])
    table.insert(1, 'sequence', served['sequence'].astype('Int64'))
    # A judge who was renominated by a new president after a recess
    # appointment was confirmed on that president's nomination.
    reappointed = served.get(
        'Reappointing President', pd.Series('', index = served.index))
    reappointed = reappointed.fillna('').str.strip()
    table['president'] = served['Appointing President'].where(
        reappointed == '', reappointed)
    table['party'] = served['Party of Appointing President'].where(
        reappointed == '',
        served.get(
            'Party of Reappointing President',
            pd.Series('', index = served.index)))
    reassigned = table['president'].str.startswith('None')
    table['reassigned'] = reassigned
    inherited = table[list(_INHERITED)].mask(reassigned)
    inherited = inherited.groupby(table['nid']).ffill()
    table[list(_INHERITED)] = inherited.where(
        reassigned, table[list(_INHERITED)]).fillna('')
    table['appointment_date'] = [
        nomination or recess or confirmation or commission
        for nomination, recess, confirmation, commission in zip(
            table['nomination_date'], table['recess_date'],
            table['confirmation_date'], table['commission_date'],
            strict = True)]
    table['circuit'] = table['court'].map(_circuit).astype('Int64')
    table['earlier'] = [
        tuple(group['court'].iloc[:position])
        for _, group in table.groupby('nid', sort = False)
        for position in range(len(group))]
    people = people.assign(nid = people['nid'].astype(int))
    people = people.drop_duplicates('nid').set_index('nid')
    names = {
        'jid': 'jid', 'last_name': 'Last Name', 'first_name': 'First Name',
        'middle_name': 'Middle Name', 'suffix': 'Suffix',
        'birth_state': 'Birth State'}
    for column, source in names.items():
        table[column] = table['nid'].map(people[source]).fillna('')
    table['jid'] = pd.to_numeric(table['jid'], errors = 'coerce').astype(
        'Int64')
    order = [
        'nid', 'jid', 'judge', 'last_name', 'first_name', 'middle_name',
        'suffix', 'sequence', 'court_type', 'court', 'title', 'circuit',
        'president', 'party', 'recess_date', 'nomination_date',
        'confirmation_date', 'commission_date', 'termination_date',
        'appointment_date', 'reassigned', 'earlier', 'birth_state']
    return table[order]

def compute(
    files: dict[str, pathlib.Path],
    *,
    senators: str = 'congress',
    martin_quinn: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    transformation: str = 'jcs2024') -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Returns the scores of the appointments and of the justices.

    Args:
        files: the path of each file, by its kind (see `sources.paths`).
        senators: which senators count, "congress" or "date" (see
            `politics.Senate.senators`). Defaults to "congress".
        martin_quinn: the file of the justices' Martin-Quinn scores.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case the one in the data folder is
            used if there is one.
        transformation: the transformation of Martin-Quinn scores, "jcs2024"
            or "paper" (see `politics.justices`). Defaults to "jcs2024".

    Returns:
        The scores of every appointment (see `scores.appointments`), and of
            every justice in every term (see `scores.justices`), which is
            empty if there are no Martin-Quinn scores. Without the file of
            duty stations, a judge whose career shows no state has the
            judge's birth state.

    """
    table = fjc.appointments(files['service'], files['demographics'])
    careers = fjc.careers(files['career'])
    found: dict[tuple[int, str], str] = {}
    if files['duty_stations'].is_file():
        found = stations.match(
            table, stations.duty_stations(files['duty_stations']))
    else:
        logger.warning(
            'there are no duty stations at %s, so judges whose careers show '
            'no state have their birth states', files['duty_stations'])
    table['duty_station'] = [
        found.get((nid, court)) for nid, court in zip(
            table['nid'], table['court'], strict = True)]
    senate = politics.Senate.from_files(
        files['congress'],
        [files['legislators_historical'], files['legislators_current']])
    path = pathlib.Path(martin_quinn) if martin_quinn else files['martin_quinn']
    terms = pd.DataFrame()
    if path.is_file():
        terms = scores.justices(
            politics.justices(path, transformation), table, start_year = 0)
    else:
        logger.warning(
            'there are no Martin-Quinn scores at %s, so the justices have no '
            'scores: save "justices.csv" from %s there', path, options._MQ_PAGE)
    scored = scores.appointments(
        table, careers, senate, start_year = None, senators = senators,
        terms = terms)
    return scored, terms

    use_published: bool = False,
    published_threshold: float = verify._PUBLISHED_THRESHOLD,
    download: bool = True,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    check: bool = True,
    session: Any = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Downloads the files that are missing, computes and checks the scores.

    Then it writes the spreadsheet (see `export.write`).

    Args:
        output: where to save the spreadsheet. Defaults to
            "judicial_common_space.xlsx" in the current folder.
        folder: the data folder. Defaults to `None`, in which case
            `utilities.data_folder()` is used.
        start_year: the first year of service to include (see
            `scores.appointments`). Defaults to 1953, the first year of
            Epstein et al.'s study. The justices' terms begin with the one
            that was sitting in January of that year (the 1952 term, for
            1953), as the study's do.
        senators: which senators count, "congress" or "date" (see
            `politics.Senate.senators`). Defaults to "congress", as in the
            published Judicial Common Space scores.
        martin_quinn: the file of the justices' Martin-Quinn scores.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case the one in the data folder is
            used, which is downloaded if it can be.
        transformation: the transformation of Martin-Quinn scores, "jcs2024"
            (as in the 2024 release of the scores) or "paper" (Epstein et
            al.'s of 2007; see `politics.justices`). Defaults to "jcs2024".
        use_published: whether to use the published score of a judge (or a
            justice's term) where it differs from the computed one by more
            than `published_threshold` (see `verify.use_published`). The
            checks still compare the computed scores. Defaults to `False`.
        published_threshold: the largest difference from a published score
            that keeps the computed score. Defaults to 0.05.
        download: whether to download the files that are missing. Defaults
            to `True`.
        overwrite: whether to download the files again even if they are
            there. Defaults to `False`.
        check: whether to compare the scores with published scores.
            Defaults to `True`.
        session: an object with a `get` method like a `requests.Session`.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case a `requests.Session` is made.

    Returns:
        The path of the spreadsheet.

    """
    files = sources.paths(folder)
    if download:
        session = utilities.open_session(session)
        sources.download(
            _INPUTS, folder, overwrite = overwrite, session = session)
        optional = ['duty_stations'] + ([] if martin_quinn else ['martin_quinn'])
        optional += list(_PUBLISHED) if check or use_published else []
        for kind in optional:
            try:
                sources.download(
                    kind, folder, overwrite = overwrite, session = session)
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                logger.warning('could not download %s: %s', kind, error)
    scored, terms = compute(
        files, senators = senators, martin_quinn = martin_quinn,
        transformation = transformation)
    checks = _checks(files, scored, terms) if check or use_published else {}
    if use_published:
        if not checks:
            logger.warning(
                'there are no published scores in %s, so every score is '
                'computed', files['jcs_judges'].parent)
        scored, terms = verify.use_published(
            scored, terms, checks, published_threshold)
        replaced = int((_since(scored, start_year)['jcs_source'] != (
            'computed')).sum())
        logger.info(
            'used the published scores of %d appointments that differ by '
            'more than %.2f', replaced, published_threshold)
    else:
        scored, terms = verify.mark_computed(scored), verify.mark_computed(
            terms)
    sheets: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {
        'Scores': _since(scored, start_year),
        # A term begins in October, so the one sitting in January of the
        # first year began the year before.
        'Justices': (
            terms[terms['term'] >= start_year - 1] if not terms.empty
            else terms)}
    if check:
        sheets['Verification'] = verify.summarize(checks)
        names = {
            'circuit_judges': 'Circuit check',
            'district_judges': 'District check',
            'justices': 'Justice check'}
        sheets.update({names[name]: table for name, table in checks.items()})
        for row in sheets['Verification'].to_dict('records'):
            logger.info(
                '%s: %d of %d found; %.1f%% the same and %.1f%% the same or '
                'within %.2f', row['check'], row['found'], row['published'],
                100 * row['share_same'], 100 * row['share_same_or_close'],
                verify._CLOSE)
    settings = {
        'start_year': start_year, 'senators': senators,
        'transformation': transformation,
        'use_published': (
            f'{use_published} (threshold {published_threshold})'
            if use_published else use_published),
        'appointments': len(sheets['Scores'])}
    path = export.write(output, sheets, settings)
    missing = int(sheets['Scores']['jcs'].isna().sum())
    logger.info(
        'wrote %d appointments to %s (%d without a score)',
        len(sheets['Scores']), path, missing)
    return path

docs.title: politics
docs.text:
Finds the NOMINATE scores of senators and presidents, and of justices.

The Judicial Common Space puts judges, justices, members of Congress, and presidents on the scale of the first dimension of NOMINATE, on which higher scores are more conservative. Voteview's DW-NOMINATE scores ("nominate_dim1" in its file of members, which courtpy uses too) are on one scale for both chambers and the president, and each member has one score for the whole of the member's service. They are the scores that the current Judicial Common Space files use.

A Senate finds the senators from a state who belonged to a president's party when a judge was appointed, in one of two ways:

  • "congress": every senator from the state who sat in the Congress of the appointment and belonged to the party (by Voteview's record of that Congress). This is how the published Judicial Common Space scores were made: in a Congress in which a senator died or resigned, the judge can get the mean of three senators.
  • "date": the senators who held the state's seats on the day of the appointment and belonged to the party on that day (by the dates of service in https://github.com/unitedstates/congress-legislators). This is the rule as Epstein et al. state it (the "home-state Senators" of "the delegation"), and is closest to how Christina Boyd made her scores of district judges.

justices puts the justices' Martin-Quinn scores on the same scale with Epstein et al.'s arctangent transformation (their equation 2).

Contents

Senate: finds the scores of senators and presidents. congress: returns the number of the Congress that sat on a day. justices: returns each justice's Judicial Common Space score in each term.

def senators(
    self,
    state: str,
    date: str,
    party: str,
    how: str = 'congress') -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    """Returns the senators of a state who belonged to a party.

    Args:
        state: the state's postal code.
        date: the day of the appointment, as YYYY-MM-DD.
        party: the president's party, "Democratic" or "Republican".
        how: "congress" for every senator who sat in the Congress of
            `date`, or "date" for the senators who served on `date`
            (see the module's documentation). Defaults to "congress".

    Raises:
        ValueError: if `how` is neither "congress" nor "date".

    Returns:
        The name and score of each senator, in Voteview's order. A
            senator without a score (who served too briefly to vote) is
            left out.

    """
    code = options._PARTY_CODES.get(party)
    if code is None or not date:
        return []
    number = congress(date)
    senate = self._senators
    rows = senate[
        (senate['congress'] == number) & (senate['state_abbrev'] == state)]
    if how == 'congress':
        rows = rows[rows['party_code'] == code]
    elif how == 'date':
        terms = self.terms
        serving = terms[
            (terms['state'] == state) & (terms['start'] <= date)
            & (terms['end'] > date) & (terms['party'] == party)]
        rows = rows[rows['bioguide_id'].isin(set(serving['bioguide']))]
        # A senator who changed parties has a row (and a score) for each
        # party in that Congress, so the row of the party is used.
        same = rows['party_code'] == code
        switched = rows['bioguide_id'].isin(
            set(rows.loc[same, 'bioguide_id']))
        rows = rows[same | ~switched]
    else:
        message = f'how must be "congress" or "date", not {how!r}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    rows = rows.drop_duplicates('icpsr')
    scores = pd.to_numeric(rows['nominate_dim1'], errors = 'coerce')
    return [
        (str(name), float(score))
        for name, score in zip(rows['bioname'], scores, strict = True)
        if not math.isnan(score)]

def congress(date: str) -> int:
    """Returns the number of the Congress that sat on a day.

    Since 1935, each Congress has begun on January 3 of an odd year; before,
    on March 4. The first Congress began in 1789.

    Args:
        date: the day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

    Returns:
        The number of the Congress.

    """
    year = int(date[:4])
    start = '01-03' if year >= 1935 else '03-04'
    if year % 2 == 1 and date[5:10] < start:
        year -= 1
    return (year - 1789) // 2 + 1

def justices(
    source: pd.DataFrame | pathlib.Path | str,
    transformation: str | tuple[float, float] = 'jcs2024') -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns each justice's Judicial Common Space score in each term.

    The score is `2 / pi * arctan(b0 + b1 * MQ)`, where MQ is the justice's
    Martin-Quinn score in the term (the mean of its estimates, "post_mn").
    Epstein et al. estimated b0 and b1 (-0.1736 and 0.461) from the
    Martin-Quinn and Common Space scores of 2005, which have both been
    rescaled since. The 2024 release of the scores used new estimates (0.1934
    and 0.6025), which put today's Martin-Quinn scores where the published
    scores are.

    Args:
        source: the "justices" file of Martin-Quinn scores, as a path or a
            table, with the columns "term", "justice", "justiceName", and
            "post_mn".
        transformation: "jcs2024" or "paper" (see `options._ARCTANGENT`), or
            the intercept and slope. Defaults to "jcs2024".

    Raises:
        KeyError: if `source` lacks a column that is needed.
        ValueError: if `transformation` is an unknown name.

    Returns:
        A table with "term" (the year in which the term began, in October),
            "justice" and "justiceName" (the Supreme Court Database's number
            and name for the justice, such as 117 and "ACBarrett"),
            "martin_quinn", and "jcs".

    """
    scores = (
        source.copy() if isinstance(source, pd.DataFrame)
        else utilities.read_csv(source))
    needed = ['term', 'justice', 'justiceName', 'post_mn']
    missing = [column for column in needed if column not in scores.columns]
    if missing:
        message = (
            f'the file of Martin-Quinn scores needs the columns {missing}, '
            f'which are missing')
        raise KeyError(message)
    if isinstance(transformation, str):
        if transformation not in options._ARCTANGENT:
            message = (
                f'transformation must be among {list(options._ARCTANGENT)}, '
                f'not {transformation!r}')
            raise ValueError(message)
        transformation = options._ARCTANGENT[transformation]
    intercept, slope = transformation
    mq = pd.to_numeric(scores['post_mn'], errors = 'coerce')
    return pd.DataFrame({
        'term': pd.to_numeric(scores['term'], errors = 'coerce').astype(
            'Int64'),
        'justice': scores['justice'],
        'justiceName': scores['justiceName'],
        'martin_quinn': mq,
        'jcs': [2 / math.pi * math.atan(intercept + slope * value)
                for value in mq]})

docs.title: scores
docs.text:
Computes the Judicial Common Space score of each appointment.

Epstein, Martin, Segal, and Westerland ("The Judicial Common Space," 23 J.L. Econ. & Org. 303 (2007)) score judges of the lower federal courts by Giles, Hettinger, and Peppers's rule, which follows the norm of senatorial courtesy: if a judge is appointed from a state where the president and at least one senator are of the same party, the judge gets that senator's NOMINATE score (or the mean of the senators' scores, if more than one is of the president's party). Otherwise, the judge gets the president's score. Justices of the Supreme Court get their Martin-Quinn scores, put on the same scale (see politics.justices).

So a judge's score belongs to an appointment: a district judge who is elevated to a court of appeals is scored again, by the president and senators of the second appointment. appointments scores every appointment to a federal court of a judge who served on it in or after a year (by default 1953, the first year of Epstein et al.'s study). A judge moved to a court without an appointment (as when the Eleventh Circuit was made from the Fifth) keeps the score of the appointment before.

Contents

appointments: returns the score of each appointment. justices: returns each justice's score in each term, with the Federal Judicial Center's numbers for the justice.

def appointments(
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    careers: Mapping[int, Sequence[str]],
    senate: politics.Senate,
    *,
    start_year: int | None = options._START_YEAR,
    senators: str = 'congress',
    terms: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the score of each appointment.

    | Column | Meaning |
    | --- | --- |
    | `judge`, `nid`, `jid` | The judge's name and the Federal Judicial Center's two numbers for the judge. |
    | `court_type`, `court`, `circuit`, `title`, `sequence` | The court, the judge's title on it, and the order of the appointment among the judge's (see `fjc.appointments`). |
    | `president`, `party` | The president who appointed the judge, and that president's party. |
    | `nomination_date`, `recess_date`, `commission_date`, `termination_date` | Dates of the appointment and of the end of the judge's service on the court. |
    | `appointment_date`, `congress` | The day that the senators and president are found on (see `fjc.appointments`), and the Congress that sat then. |
    | `reassigned` | Whether the judge was moved to the court without an appointment, and so keeps the score of the appointment before. |
    | `home_state`, `state_source` | The state that the judge was appointed from (a postal code), and how it was found (see `states.home_state`). |
    | `duty_station` | For a judge of a court of appeals, the state where Wikipedia says the judge sat (see `stations`), which is used for `home_state` only when the judge's career shows none. |
    | `method` | How the score was found: "home-state senator", "home-state senators", "president", or "Martin-Quinn". |
    | `senators` | The senators whose scores were used, separated by semicolons. |
    | `president_score` | The president's score. |
    | `jcs` | The Judicial Common Space score. A justice's score is that of the first term of the appointment (`justices` has every term). Missing if there is no score (as for Herbert Hoover, whom Voteview does not score, or a justice without Martin-Quinn scores). |

    Args:
        table: the appointments (see `fjc.appointments`), with the states of
            the judges' duty stations as "duty_station" if they are known
            (see `stations.match`).
        careers: the entries of each judge's career, by the judge's "nid"
            (see `fjc.careers`).
        senate: the scores of senators and presidents.
        start_year: the first year of service to include: an appointment is
            included if the judge was serving on the court in that year or
            later. Defaults to 1953. `None` includes every appointment.
        senators: "congress" or "date": which senators count (see
            `politics.Senate.senators`). Defaults to "congress", as in the
            published Judicial Common Space scores.
        terms: the justices' scores in each term (see `justices`). Defaults
            to `None`, in which case the justices have no scores.

    Returns:
        The table, sorted by the judges' names and the order of their
            appointments.

    """
    first_terms = {} if terms is None else _first_terms(terms)
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    previous: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    records = cast('list[dict[str, Any]]', table.to_dict('records'))
    for record in records:
        if previous is not None and previous['nid'] != record['nid']:
            previous = None
        row = {column: record.get(column) for column in _COLUMNS}
        date = str(record['appointment_date'] or '')
        row['congress'] = politics.congress(date) if date else None
        if record['reassigned'] and previous is not None:
            for column in (
                'home_state', 'state_source', 'method', 'senators',
                'president_score', 'jcs'):
                row[column] = previous[column]
        else:
            row.update(_score(record, careers, senate, senators, first_terms))
        rows.append(row)
        previous = row
    scored = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns = list(_COLUMNS))
    if start_year is not None:
        first = f'{start_year}-01-01'
        serving = (scored['termination_date'] == '') | (
            scored['termination_date'] >= first)
        scored = scored[serving]
    scored = scored.sort_values(['judge', 'nid', 'sequence'], kind = 'stable')
    scored = scored.astype({
        'circuit': 'Int64', 'sequence': 'Int64', 'congress': 'Int64',
        'jcs': 'Float64', 'president_score': 'Float64'})
    return scored.reset_index(drop = True)

def justices(
    terms: pd.DataFrame,
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    start_year: int = options._START_YEAR) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns each justice's score in each term, with the center's numbers.

    Each justice of the Martin-Quinn scores is found among the Supreme Court
    appointments of `table` by the justice's last name and initials (the
    Supreme Court Database names justices like "WHRehnquist"). A term belongs
    to the justice's last appointment that was commissioned by the end of
    the term (the June after it began), so William Rehnquist's terms from
    1986 are those of his appointment as Chief Justice.

    Args:
        terms: the justices' scores in each term (see `politics.justices`).
        table: the appointments (see `fjc.appointments`).
        start_year: the first term to include. Defaults to 1953.

    Returns:
        A table with "term", "justiceName", "judge", "nid", "jid", "title"
            (the justice's title in the term), "sequence" (of the
            appointment), "martin_quinn", and "jcs".

    """
    court = table[table['court_type'] == 'Supreme Court']
    found = _justice_numbers(
        court, [str(name) for name in terms['justiceName'].unique()])
    rows = []
    for record in terms.to_dict('records'):
        term = record['term']
        nid = found.get(record['justiceName'])
        if term is None or pd.isna(term) or int(term) < start_year:
            continue
        appointment = None
        if nid is not None:
            served = court[
                (court['nid'] == nid)
                & (court['commission_date'] != '')
                & (court['commission_date'] <= f'{int(term) + 1}-06-30')]
            if len(served):
                appointment = served.iloc[-1]
        rows.append({
            'term': int(term),
            'justiceName': record['justiceName'],
            'judge': None if appointment is None else appointment['judge'],
            'nid': nid,
            'jid': None if appointment is None else appointment['jid'],
            'title': None if appointment is None else appointment['title'],
            'sequence': (
                None if appointment is None else appointment['sequence']),
            'martin_quinn': record['martin_quinn'],
            'jcs': record['jcs']})
    result = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if result.empty:
        return result
    result = result.astype({'nid': 'Int64', 'jid': 'Int64', 'sequence': 'Int64'})
    return result.sort_values(['term', 'justiceName']).reset_index(drop = True)

def download(
    kinds: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
    folder: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    session: Any = None) -> dict[str, pathlib.Path]:
    """Downloads the files that are missing.

    Args:
        kinds: the files to download (see the module's documentation).
            Defaults to `None`, for all of them.
        folder: the data folder. Defaults to `None`, in which case
            `utilities.data_folder()` is used.
        overwrite: whether to download a file that is already there. The
            Federal Judicial Center adds judges as they are appointed, and
            Voteview changes the scores of sitting members as they vote.
            Defaults to `False`.
        session: an object with a `get` method like a `requests.Session`.
            Defaults to `None`, in which case a `requests.Session` is made.

    Raises:
        requests.HTTPError: if a page or a file cannot be downloaded.
        ValueError: if one of `kinds` is unknown, or a page has no link to
            its file.

    Returns:
        The path of each file, by its kind.

    """
    wanted = (
        list(_NAMES) if kinds is None
        else [kinds] if isinstance(kinds, str) else list(kinds))
    unknown = [kind for kind in wanted if kind not in _NAMES]
    if unknown:
        message = f'kinds must be among {list(_NAMES)}, not {unknown}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    found = paths(folder)
    session = utilities.open_session(session)
    archive_needed = False
    for kind in wanted:
        path = found[kind]
        if path.is_file() and not overwrite:
            continue
        if kind in options._FJC_FILES:
            utilities.download_file(
                options._FJC_URL + _NAMES[kind], path, overwrite = True,
                session = session)
        elif kind == 'congress':
            utilities.download_file(
                options._VOTEVIEW_URL + _NAMES[kind], path, overwrite = True,
                session = session)
        elif kind in options._LEGISLATORS_FILES:
            utilities.download_file(
                options._LEGISLATORS_URL + _NAMES[kind], path,
                overwrite = True, session = session)
        elif kind == 'martin_quinn':
            utilities.download_file(
                _link(options._MQ_PAGE, options._MQ_FILE, session), path,
                overwrite = True, session = session)
        elif kind == 'boyd':
            utilities.download_file(
                options._BOYD_URL, path, overwrite = True, session = session)
        elif kind == 'duty_stations':
            _download_wikipedia(path, session)
        else:
            archive_needed = True
    if archive_needed:
        _unpack_jcs(found, session)
    return {kind: found[kind] for kind in wanted}

docs.title: states
docs.text:
Finds the state that each judge was appointed from.

Giles, Hettinger, and Peppers's rule gives a judge the scores of the senators of the judge's home state, so each appointment needs a state. The Federal Judicial Center's files name it for a district judge (in the court's name), but not for a judge of a court of appeals, which serves several states. Its place is found from the judge's record, in this order:

  1. The state of a district court that the judge served on before, if it is in the circuit.
  2. The judge's career before the appointment (see career_state): the jobs that the judge held when appointed come first, then the most recent jobs before. A job's place is the first state that its entry names (as in "Federal Public Defender for the Districts of Colorado and Wyoming"), not counting cities and counties named for states ("Kansas City, Missouri"), or else the state of a city or school that it names without one (as "Harvard Law School"; see options._PLACES). Only states of the circuit count.
  3. The state of the judge's duty station, as Wikipedia's article on the court gives it (see stations), if it is in the circuit. It comes after the judge's career because it is where the judge sat, which is sometimes not where the judge came from (Alfred Goodwin came from Oregon's district court and sat in California).
  4. The state where the judge was born, if it is in the circuit.

Judges of the District of Columbia Circuit have the District of Columbia, which has no senators, so they get the score of the president, as all but three of them do in the published Judicial Common Space scores (even those who came from district courts in states). Judges of courts with national jurisdiction (the Federal Circuit, the Court of International Trade, and the courts before them) have no home state, so they get the score of the president too, as the Federal Circuit's judges do in the published scores.

Contents

def career_state(
    entries: Sequence[str],
    year: int,
    allowed: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    *,
    past: bool = True) -> str | None:
    """Returns the state of a judge's career before an appointment.

    The jobs that the judge held in the year of the appointment come first
    (the most recent first, and minor ones such as visiting professorships
    last), then the jobs that had ended (the most recent first).

    Args:
        entries: the entries of the judge's career (see `fjc.careers`).
        year: the year of the appointment.
        allowed: the states that count. Defaults to `None`, for all of them.
        past: whether jobs that had ended by the appointment count.
            Defaults to `True`.

    Returns:
        The postal code of the state, or `None` if no entry names one that
            counts.

    """
    permitted = None if allowed is None else set(allowed)
    current: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    minor: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    ended: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
    for entry in entries:
        start, end = _span(entry)
        if start is None or start > year:
            continue
        if end is None or end >= year:
            if options._MINOR_POSITIONS.match(entry):
                minor.append((start, entry))
            else:
                current.append((start, entry))
        else:
            ended.append((end, start, entry))
    ordered = (
        [entry for _, entry in sorted(current, key = lambda x: -x[0])]
        + [entry for _, entry in sorted(minor, key = lambda x: -x[0])])
    if past:
        ordered += [
            entry for _, _, entry in sorted(
                ended, key = lambda x: (-x[0], -x[1]))]
    for entry in ordered:
        for state in places(entry):
            if permitted is None or state in permitted:
                return state
    return None

def home_state(
    appointment: Mapping[str, Any],
    career: Sequence[str] = ()) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Returns the state that a judge was appointed from, and how it was found.

    Args:
        appointment: a row of `fjc.appointments`, with the state of the
            judge's duty station as "duty_station" if it is known (see
            `stations.match`).
        career: the entries of the judge's career (see `fjc.careers`).

    Returns:
        The postal code of the state (`None` if there is none), and how it
            was found: "court" (the court's name), "earlier district court",
            "career", "duty station", "birth state", "national court",
            "Supreme Court", or "not found".

    """
    court = str(appointment['court'])
    court_type = str(appointment['court_type'])
    if court_type == 'U.S. District Court':
        return _district_state(court), 'court'
    if court_type == 'Supreme Court':
        return None, 'Supreme Court'
    try:
        circuit: int | None = int(appointment.get('circuit'))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        circuit = None
    national = any(name in court for name in options._NATIONAL_COURTS)
    if circuit is None or circuit == 13 or national:
        return None, 'national court'
    date = str(appointment.get('appointment_date') or '')
    year = int(date[:4]) if date else 9999
    if circuit == 12:
        return 'DC', 'court'
    if circuit == 5 and date and date < options._SPLIT_FIFTH:
        allowed = options._OLD_FIFTH
    else:
        allowed = options._CIRCUIT_STATES[circuit]
    for earlier in reversed(list(appointment.get('earlier') or ())):
        state = _district_state(str(earlier))
        if state and state in allowed:
            return state, 'earlier district court'
    state = career_state(career, year, allowed)
    if state:
        return state, 'career'
    station = str(appointment.get('duty_station') or '')
    if station in allowed:
        return station, 'duty station'
    birth = str(appointment.get('birth_state') or '')
    if birth in allowed:
        return birth, 'birth state'
    return None, 'not found'

def places(entry: str) -> list[str]:
    """Returns the states that a career entry names.

    Args:
        entry: an entry of a judge's career.

    Returns:
        The postal codes of the states, most likely first: the states that
            the entry names, in its order (leaving out names of cities and
            counties, as in "Kansas City, Missouri"); then the states of
            cities and schools that it names without their states; then "DC"
            if it names Washington, D.C., or a job that is there (see
            `options._DC_AGENCIES`).

    """
    text = entry
    capital = False
    for pattern in (options._DC_PLACES, options._DC_AGENCIES):
        if pattern.search(text):
            capital = True
            text = pattern.sub(' ', text)
    implied: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
    for pattern, state in (*_NOT_THEIR_STATES, *options._PLACES):
        for match in pattern.finditer(text):
            implied.append((match.start(), state))
        text = pattern.sub(lambda match: ' ' * len(match.group()), text)
    named = [
        _ABBREVIATIONS[match.group(1)] for match in _NAMES.finditer(text)
        if not _NOT_A_STATE.match(text, match.end())]
    found = named + [state for _, state in sorted(implied)]
    if capital:
        found.append('DC')
    return list(dict.fromkeys(found))

Finds where the judges of the courts of appeals sat, from Wikipedia.

The Federal Judicial Center does not record the state that a judge of a court of appeals came from or sat in. If no row fits, or the rows that fit name different states, the appointment has none. A judge moved to a court without an appointment is not matched, since the judge keeps the home state of the appointment before.

def match(
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    stations: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[tuple[int, str], str]:
    """Returns the Wikipedia state of each appointment to a court of appeals.

    An appointment is the row of `stations` on the same court whose service
    began within a year of the appointment's commission (or recess
    appointment) and whose name contains every word of the judge's last
    name. If no row fits, or the rows that fit name different states, the
    appointment has none. A judge moved to a court without an appointment is
    not matched, since the judge keeps the home state of the appointment
    before.

    Args:
        table: the appointments (see `fjc.appointments`).
        stations: the judges' states (see `duty_stations`).

    Returns:
        The postal code of the state of each appointment that was matched,
            by the judge's "nid" and the court's name.

    """
    names = [set(_words(name)) for name in stations['name']]
    found = {}
    appeals = table[
        (table['court_type'] == 'U.S. Court of Appeals')
        & ~table['reassigned'].astype(bool)]
    for record in appeals.to_dict('records'):
        began = str(record['commission_date'] or record['recess_date'])[:4]
        last = set(_words(str(record['last_name'])))
        if not began.isdigit() or not last or pd.isna(record['circuit']):
            continue
        fits = {
            state for circuit, start, state, words in zip(
                stations['circuit'], stations['start'], stations['state'],
                names, strict = True)
            if circuit == record['circuit'] and abs(start - int(began)) <= 1
            and last <= words}
        if len(fits) == 1:
            found[(int(record['nid']), str(record['court']))] = fits.pop()
    return found

def parse(wikitext: str) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Returns the judges in the source text of one article.

    Args:
        wikitext: the article's source text.

    Returns:
        The "name", "start" (the first year of the judge's service on the
            court), and "state" (a postal code) of each judge whose row
            gives all three. A row is read up to the start of the next one,
            so a footnote that spans lines does not cut it short.

    """
    starts = [found.end() for found in _ROW.finditer(wikitext)]
    rows = []
    for begin, end in zip(starts, [*starts[1:], len(wikitext)], strict = True):
        fields = dict(_FIELD.findall(wikitext[begin:end]))
        written = fields.get('name', '')
        sortname = _SORTNAME.search(written)
        name = (
            f'{sortname.group(1)} {sortname.group(2)}' if sortname
            else ' '.join(_LINK.findall(written)) or written)
        place = fields.get('state') or fields.get('duty station') or ''
        shown = ' '.join(_LINK.findall(place)) or place
        # "Greenville, SC" and "VA" both end with the state's postal code.
        state = shown.split(',')[-1].strip().replace('.', '').upper()
        start = re.search(r'\d{4}', fields.get('term', ''))
        if name.strip() and start and state in options._STATES:
            rows.append({
                'name': name.strip(), 'start': int(start.group()),
                'state': state})
    return rows

docs.text:
Compares the scores with published scores.

Check Published scores Matched by circuit_judges The Judicial Common Space scores of the judges of the courts of appeals (Epstein et al.'s "coa_judges" file, from https://epstein.wustl.edu/jcs). The judge's name and circuit (see match_name). district_judges Christina Boyd's scores of district judges, made by the same rule from the Federal Judicial Center's list of judges and Voteview's scores. The center's "nid". justices The Judicial Common Space scores of the justices in each term (the "supreme_court_long" file). The term and the Supreme Court Database's name for the justice.

use_published can put the published score in place of a computed one that differs from it by more than 0.05 (--use-published).

Each comparison is "same" if the scores differ by less than 0.0005 (the rounding of NOMINATE scores to three places), "close" if they differ by less than 0.02, and "different" otherwise. Voteview estimates the scores of every member who is serving again whenever it adds a Congress, so the scores of a judge whose senators or president are still in office drift a little from those that were published with an older file: such differences are "close".

Contents

circuit_judges: compares the scores of judges of the courts of appeals. district_judges: compares the scores of district judges. justices: compares the scores of justices in each term. mark_computed: adds the columns that say where each score came from. match_name: returns the "nid" of a judge in the Judicial Common Space file of judges. summarize: returns the agreement of each comparison. use_published: uses the published scores that differ from the computed ones.

def circuit_judges(
    scored: pd.DataFrame,
    published: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compares the scores of judges of the courts of appeals.

    Args:
        scored: the scores of the appointments (see
            `scores.appointments`), with the judges' names.
        published: the published scores, with the columns "name",
            "circuit", and "jcs".

    Returns:
        A row for each judge of the published file, with "name", "circuit",
            "nid", "published", "computed", "difference", "agreement", and
            how the computed score was found.

    """
    appeals = scored[scored['court_type'] == 'U.S. Court of Appeals']
    rows = []
    for record in published.to_dict('records'):
        name, circuit = str(record['name']), int(record['circuit'])
        name, circuit = _CORRECTIONS.get((name, circuit), (name, circuit))
        court = appeals[appeals['circuit'] == circuit]
        nid = match_name(name, court)
        mine = court[court['nid'] == nid].head(1)
        rows.append({
            'name': record['name'], 'circuit': circuit, 'nid': nid,
            **_compare(record['jcs'], mine)})
    return _finish(pd.DataFrame(rows))

def district_judges(
    scored: pd.DataFrame,
    published: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compares the scores of district judges.

    A judge who was appointed to more than one district court has one score
    in the published file, which is compared with that of the judge's first
    appointment to a district court.

    Args:
        scored: the scores of the appointments (see `scores.appointments`).
        published: Boyd's scores, with the columns "nid", "judgename", and
            "ideology_score".

    Returns:
        A row for each judge of the published file, with "name", "nid",
            "published", "computed", "difference", "agreement", and how the
            computed score was found.

    """
    district = scored[
        (scored['court_type'] == 'U.S. District Court')
        & ~scored['reassigned'].astype(bool)]
    district = district.sort_values(['nid', 'sequence'])
    rows = []
    for record in published.to_dict('records'):
        nid = pd.to_numeric(record['nid'], errors = 'coerce')
        nid = None if pd.isna(nid) else int(nid)
        mine = district[district['nid'] == nid].head(1)
        rows.append({
            'name': record['judgename'], 'nid': nid,
            'court': mine['court'].iloc[0] if len(mine) else None,
            **_compare(record['ideology_score'], mine)})
    return _finish(pd.DataFrame(rows))

def justices(
    terms: pd.DataFrame,
    published: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compares the scores of justices in each term.

    Args:
        terms: the justices' scores (see `scores.justices`).
        published: the published scores, with the columns "term",
            "justiceName", and "jcs".

    Returns:
        A row for each justice and term of the published file, with "term",
            "justiceName", "judge", "nid", "published", "computed",
            "difference", and "agreement".

    """
    mine = terms[['term', 'justiceName', 'judge', 'nid', 'jcs']].rename(
        columns = {'jcs': 'computed'})
    theirs = published[['term', 'justiceName', 'jcs']].rename(
        columns = {'jcs': 'published'})
    theirs = theirs.assign(term = pd.to_numeric(theirs['term']).astype(int))
    merged = theirs.merge(mine, on = ['term', 'justiceName'], how = 'left')
    merged['difference'] = merged['computed'] - merged['published']
    return _finish(merged)

def mark_computed(table: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Adds the columns that say where each score came from.

    Args:
        table: scores of appointments (see `scores.appointments`) or of
            justices' terms (see `scores.justices`), with a "jcs" column.

    Returns:
        A copy of the table with "computed_jcs" (the computed score) before
            "jcs" and "jcs_source" ("computed") after it, unless it has them.

    """
    table = table.copy()
    if 'jcs' not in table.columns or 'jcs_source' in table.columns:
        return table
    table.insert(list(table.columns).index('jcs'), 'computed_jcs', table['jcs'])
    table.insert(list(table.columns).index('jcs') + 1, 'jcs_source', 'computed')
    return table

The judge is the one judge of court whose last name is the file's (or contains its words, as "Barrett, Amy Coney" contains "Coney Barrett"), told apart from others with the same last name by the first name or initial, and then by the suffix.

def match_name(name: str, court: pd.DataFrame) -> int | None:
    """Returns the "nid" of a judge in the Judicial Common Space file of judges.

    The file names a judge as "Last, First Middle" (with any suffix, such as
    "Jr.", after another comma). The judge is the one judge of `court`
    whose last name is the file's (or contains its words, as "Barrett, Amy
    Coney" contains "Coney Barrett"), told apart from others with the same
    last name by the first name or initial, and then by the suffix.

    Args:
        name: the judge's name in the file.
        court: the appointments to the judge's court (see
            `scores.appointments`), with the judges' names.

    Returns:
        The judge's "nid", or `None` if no judge or more than one fits.

    """
    last, _, rest = name.partition(',')
    surname = _words(last)
    given = [word for word in _words(rest) if word not in _SUFFIXES]
    suffixes = [word for word in _words(rest) if word in _SUFFIXES]
    people = court.drop_duplicates('nid')
    fits = []
    for person in people.to_dict('records'):
        theirs = _words(str(person['judge']).partition(',')[0])
        everything = set(_words(str(person['judge'])))
        if surname == theirs or (
            len(surname) > 1 and set(surname) <= everything) or (
            ''.join(surname) == ''.join(theirs)):
            fits.append(person)
    if len(fits) > 1 and given:
        first = given[0]
        # A first name may be an initial or short for the center's ("Sam"
        # for "Samuel").
        named = [
            person for person in fits
            if any(
                word == first or (len(first) == 1 and word[0] == first)
                or (len(first) > 2 and word.startswith(first))
                for word in _words(str(person['judge']).partition(',')[2]))]
        fits = named or fits
    if len(fits) > 1 and suffixes:
        fits = [
            person for person in fits
            if suffixes[0] in _words(str(person['judge']).partition(',')[2])]
    return int(fits[0]['nid']) if len(fits) == 1 else None

def summarize(checks: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Returns the agreement of each comparison.

    Args:
        checks: the results of `circuit_judges`, `district_judges`, and
            `justices`, by the name of each check.

    Returns:
        A row for each check, with the number of published scores, the
            number that were found, and the number and share of those that
            are the same, close, and different, the correlation of the
            scores (missing if either set does not vary), and the mean
            absolute difference.

    """
    rows = []
    for name, check in checks.items():
        found = check[check['agreement'] != 'not found']
        counts = found['agreement'].value_counts()
        total = max(len(found), 1)
        published = found['published'].astype(float)
        computed = found['computed'].astype(float)
        varied = len(found) > 1 and published.std() > 0 and computed.std() > 0
        rows.append({
            'check': name,
            'published': len(check),
            'found': len(found),
            'same': int(counts.get('same', 0)),
            'close': int(counts.get('close', 0)),
            'different': int(counts.get('different', 0)),
            'share_same': counts.get('same', 0) / total,
            'share_same_or_close': (
                counts.get('same', 0) + counts.get('close', 0)) / total,
            'correlation': published.corr(computed) if varied else None,
            'mean_absolute_difference': (
                found['difference'].astype(float).abs().mean()
                if len(found) else None)})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def use_published(
    scored: pd.DataFrame,
    terms: pd.DataFrame,
    checks: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame],
    threshold: float = _PUBLISHED_THRESHOLD) -> tuple[
        pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Uses the published scores that differ from the computed ones.

    Where a published score and the computed one differ by more than
    `threshold`, the appointment (or the justice's term) gets the published
    score, and "jcs_source" names where it came from: "Epstein et al." for
    the Judicial Common Space scores of circuit judges and justices, and
    "Boyd" for district judges. The appointment that gets it is the one that
    the check compared (see `circuit_judges` and `district_judges`). A
    justice's appointment gets the published score of its first term if that
    term's score was replaced.

    Args:
        scored: the scores of the appointments (see `scores.appointments`).
        terms: the justices' scores (see `scores.justices`).
        checks: the results of `circuit_judges`, `district_judges`, and
            `justices`, by the name of each check. Checks that are missing
            change nothing.
        threshold: the largest difference that keeps the computed score.
            Defaults to 0.05.

    Returns:
        The two tables, with "computed_jcs" and "jcs_source" (see
            `mark_computed`).

    """
    scored = mark_computed(scored)
    terms = mark_computed(terms)

    def large(name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        check = checks.get(name)
        if check is None or check.empty:
            return pd.DataFrame()
        difference = pd.to_numeric(check['difference'], errors = 'coerce')
        return check[difference.abs() > threshold]

    for row in large('circuit_judges').to_dict('records'):
        rows = scored.index[
            (scored['court_type'] == 'U.S. Court of Appeals')
            & (scored['nid'] == row['nid'])
            & (scored['circuit'] == row['circuit'])][:1]
        _replace(scored, rows, row['published'], 'Epstein et al.')
    for row in large('district_judges').to_dict('records'):
        district = scored[
            (scored['court_type'] == 'U.S. District Court')
            & ~scored['reassigned'].astype(bool)
            & (scored['nid'] == row['nid'])]
        rows = district.sort_values('sequence').index[:1]
        _replace(scored, rows, row['published'], 'Boyd')
    for row in large('justices').to_dict('records'):
        rows = terms.index[
            (terms['term'] == row['term'])
            & (terms['justiceName'] == row['justiceName'])]
        _replace(terms, rows, row['published'], 'Epstein et al.')
    if not terms.empty and 'jcs_source' in terms.columns:
        known = terms.dropna(subset = ['nid', 'sequence']).sort_values('term')
        first = known.drop_duplicates(['nid', 'sequence'])
        first = first[first['jcs_source'] != 'computed']
        for row in first.to_dict('records'):
            rows = scored.index[
                (scored['court_type'] == 'Supreme Court')
                & (scored['nid'] == row['nid'])
                & (scored['sequence'] == row['sequence'])]
            _replace(scored, rows, row['jcs'], row['jcs_source'])
    return scored, terms
